notes: The two attached images (glitter dolphin and elephant statues) are only inspiration photos for colour-changing statues; they contain no circuit and were not used.
No breadboard is used; the manual solders wires directly to the Nano Every pads/headers, so all wire ends are 'solder' joins. Jumper-wire type is used for every wire per instructions.

The manual does not state which Nano GND pad feeds the LED strip; assumed the Nano's second GND pin (GND.2), which is the same net as GND.1. The strip GND wire is implied by the strip's three labels (VDC, DIN, GND).
The DS3231 module has a 4-pin pass-through on its other side, modelled as P.* ports conducting to the primary pins; the BME280 is wired from this side in matching order (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL).

Wire colours: 3V3 red, GND black, SDA (A4) blue, SCL (A5) yellow, 5V to strip red, D7 to DIN white; the colours of the RTC-to-BME280 wires and the strip GND wire are assumed to match the same convention.
Power is via USB (usb-cable joined to the Nano USB port); the cable's far end (PC/power bank) is not modelled.
The 3D-printed gnome enclosure (lower and upper STL parts) is not in the catalogue and is not modelled as parts.
The strip is the 8-LED WS2812B strip; DOUT is left unconnected.
